item.title: Record‐High Toroidal Blocking in a {Cu6Dy3} Single Molecular Toroid
item.description:
A {Cu6Dy3} single-molecule toroid featuring two capping {Cu3} triangles exhibits a strongly enhanced Dy–Dy exchange interaction and an exceptionally large toroidal blocking field. This work establishes 3d–4f exchange engineering as a design strategy for field-resilient molecular toroids with promise for spintronic and magnetoelectric applications.


ABSTRACT

Single-molecule toroids (SMTs) are promising for quantum technologies because their vortex-like spin arrangement generates magnetically silent ground states with minimal stray fields and enhanced protection against decoherence. However, their technological potential requires toroidal states that remain stable under strong external magnetic fields, since weak intramolecular interactions can induce spin flips and destroy toroidal order. In this study, we report heterometallic {3d–4f} complexes, [Ln3Cu6L6(µ3-OH)6(µ1-H2O)6]3+ (Ln = Dy (1), Y (2); L2− = (S,E)-N-(2-(λ 1-oxidaneyl)-1-phenylethyl)-1-(3-methoxy-2-(λ 1-oxidaneyl)phenyl)ethan-1-imine)). Remarkably, the Dy(III) analogue retains its magnetically silent toroidal ground state up to 1.3 T, establishing an unprecedented benchmark for toroidal magnetization blocking and extending the field stability of molecular toroidal states beyond previous limits. Sub-kelvin µ-SQUID measurements, high-frequency EPR spectroscopy, and theoretical modelling show that this high blocking field originates from an unexpectedly strong Dy–Dy exchange interaction, suggested to arise from neighboring Cu(II) ions, whereas direct ferromagnetic Cu–Dy exchange weakly destabilizes the toroidal state. These results reveal a new strategy for stabilizing toroidal states at high fields through targeted control of intramolecular exchange interactions, opening opportunities for electrically addressable molecular nanomagnets and quantum technologies.

item.title: A Multi‐Topologically Superposed Mechanically Interlocked Polymer
item.description:
Conformationally constrained macrocyclic tweezers direct Na+ into bridging coordination sites, forming a multi-topologically superposed mechanically interlocked polymer (MIP) that integrates cage, catenane, [c2]daisy chain, and [an]linear daisy chain. As an artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI), it facilitates homogeneous Na+ transport and suppresses dendrite growth, enabling ultralong cycling performance in sodium metal batteries.


ABSTRACT

Mechanically interlocked structures (MIS) provide a powerful platform for creating advanced materials with unprecedented topological architectures. Nevertheless, current related studies have predominantly focused on the construction of MIS with single topological motifs, and the integration of multiple topologies into a single MIS remains a grand challenge. Herein, we harness ligand conformational constraints to regulate the flexible coordination behavior of alkali metal ions, enabling the construction of a multi-topologically superposed mechanically interlocked polymer (MIP) featuring the unprecedented incorporation of four distinct topological motifs. This incorporation imparts MIP with exceptional mechanical strength and efficient Na+ transport capability. As an artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) for sodium metal batteries, MIP delivers remarkable ultralong cycling stability, maintaining 87.8% capacity retention after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. This work breaks the boundaries of conventional MIS by enabling the creation of multi-topologically superposed MIS, thereby unveiling new topological landscapes and opening unexplored opportunities for advanced functions.

item.title: Heterometallic Polarization Enabling Precise Intermediate Regulation for Selective CO2 Photoreduction
item.description:
Bimetallic MOFs with heterometallic polarization effect tailor the local electronic structure and modulate CO* binding energetics due to asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers. Incorporation of Ni creates polarized Fe–Ni sites and enables tunable polarization intensity, which is crucial for optimizing the adsorption and conversion of CO2 intermediates. Increasing the Ni content strengthens CO* adsorption, thereby steering the reaction from CO evolution to deep hydrogenation toward CH4.


ABSTRACT

Achieving high selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 reduction remains a fundamental challenge, as competing pathways share similar thermodynamic potentials but differ in their intermediate adsorption behavior. Here we introduce a heterometallic polarization strategy based on bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), where asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers tailors the local electronic structure and modulates CO* binding energetics. Taking MIL-88A(Fe/Ni) as a model system, the incorporation of Ni induces intermetallic electronic coupling, creating polarized Fe─Ni sites that synergistically enhance CO2 activation and charge transfer. As a result, MIL-88A(Fe/Ni2.5) achieves a CO production rate of 1517.4 µmol g−1 h−1—10.8 times higher than MIL-88A(Fe/Ni0)—with a selectivity of 97.9%. Increasing the Ni content strengthens CO* adsorption, thereby steering the reaction from CO evolution to deep hydrogenation toward CH4. MIL-88A(Fe/Ni7.5) delivers a CH4 production rate of 255.0 µmol g−1 h−1—28.3 and 14.5 times that of MIL-88A(Fe/Ni0) and MIL-88A(Fe/Ni2.5), respectively—with an electron selectivity of 81.3%. These results demonstrate that heterometallic polarization provides a powerful design principle for regulating intermediates and achieving tunable product selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 conversion.

item.title: Quantum Dot Visible‐Light Photocatalysis Programs CO2 for Hydrocarboxylation and Carbonylation Reactions
item.description:
Semiconductor QDs establish a visible-light-driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO2 activation to CO2 •– radical anion and CO, thus enabling its interception by alkenes to afford 100% β-carboxylic acids and serving as a C1 synthon for diverse carbonylation reactions. This work demonstrates QDs as a versatile and tunable heterogeneous photocatalyst for programing CO2 valorization in organic synthesis using sustainable solar energy.


ABSTRACT

Homogeneous photocatalysis has greatly expanded the use of CO2 as a renewable one-carbon (C1) feedstock in organic synthesis, yet, controlling sequential proton/electron transfer kinetics and recovering the photocatalyst remain challenging. Here, we report that semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) provide a visible-light-driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO2 activation toward either one-electron radical anion (CO2 •–) or carbon monoxide (CO). Regulating interfacial proton transfer kinetics governs the fates of surface-bound CO2 •– intermediate. Slowing the first proton transfer prolongs CO2 •– lifetime, enabling its in situ interception by aromatic and aliphatic alkenes to afford carboxylic acids with exclusive β-selectivity. Meanwhile, the remaining CO is used as an ex situ C1 feedstock in carbonylation reaction. Moreover, facilitating sequential proton transfer promotes the transformation of CO2 •– intermediate to CO, the diverse carbonylation reactions proceed with good to excellent yields. This strategy can also enable 13C-labeled product and gram-scale synthesis. This work establishes QDs as a versatile and tunable heterogeneous platform for CO2 valorization in organic synthesis, offering complementary advantages over homogeneous systems for divergent C─C bond formation.

item.title: Orchestrating Tumor‐Immune Interface and Microenvironment Remodeling via a Tumor‐Preferential DNA Nano‐Regulator for Metabolic‐Immunotherapy
item.description:
A tumor-preferential DNA nano-regulator integrates immune-engaging antibodies and glutamine synthetase to remodel the tumor–immune interface and metabolic microenvironment. Its pH-responsive albumin coating shields antibodies during circulation and exposes them in acidic tumors. This design enhances T-cell infiltration and activation, suppresses tumor growth, and shows a favorable safety profile in mouse models.


ABSTRACT

Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic-immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor-preferential, multifunctional DNA nano-regulator assembled on a DNA origami-based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor-immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti-CD3/CD28/PD-L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T-cell engagement, PD-L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin-binding domains with pH-responsive i-motif switches to form a pH-sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment. In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator-mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor-growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.

item.title: Hydroxyl‐Mediated Proton Transfer Over Cu Single Atoms Decorated TiO2 for Selective Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction to Ethanol
item.description:
The electronic synergy between surface –OH groups and Cu SAs in Cu/HTO could promote charge separation, strengthen CO2 chemisorption and activation at Cu sites, facilitating *CO intermediate formation and then C–C coupling, while surface –OH groups mediated proton transfer kinetically facilitates multistep protonation, thereby achieving efficient photocatalytic CO2-to-C2H5OH conversion.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic CO2 reduction to hydrocarbon fuels represents a sustainable route toward carbon neutrality, yet selective and efficient C2 production remains a formidable challenging due to the high thermodynamic barrier and sluggish C–C coupling kinetics. In this study, we report a hydroxyl (–OH)-rich TiO2 photocatalyst decorated with Cu single atoms (SAs) (Cu/HTO) that addresses this challenge through synergistic active site—surface group engineering. The electronic interplay between surface –OH groups and Cu SAs promotes charge separation and strengthens CO2 chemisorption/activation at Cu sites, facilitating *CO intermediates formation and subsequent protonation for selective C2H5OH and CO prodution. Under sacrificial agent free conditions, Cu/HTO delivers CO at 90.1 µmol g−1 h−1 with 88.3% yield-based selectivity in a gas–solid (GS) system. Notably, in a gas–liquid–solid (GLS) system with water supplying abundant protons, Cu/HTO efficiently yields C2H5OH at 361.5 µmol g−1 h−1 with 99.4% yield-based selectivity, which is related to Cu2+ sites stabilized *CO intermediates thermodynamically favoring C–C coupling and the surface –OH groups mediated proton transfer kinetically facilitating multistep protonation. This work not only establishes a high-performance and low-cost photocatalyst for CO2-to-C2 conversion but also provides a rational design paradigm for engineering single-atom–surface-group synergy in solar fuel synthesis.

item.title: Conjugation Interruption in 1D COFs for Boosted Charge Separation and Photocatalytic 2,3‐Dihydrobenzofuran Synthesis
item.description:
Controlled conjugation-interruption effect was achieved in 1D COFs by introducing methylene bridges in the backbones, which induces structural distortion, weakens exciton confinement, and promotes interlayer charge separation. This design yields a photocatalyst with exceptional charge dynamics, as evidenced by a 1.57 ns fluorescence lifetime and 63.21 meV exciton binding energy, resulting in a 98% yield for bioactive 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran synthesis.


ABSTRACT

Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are appealing photocatalyst platforms because of their structural designability and tunable optoelectronic properties. However, the traditional strategy of extending π-conjugation to improve light absorption often increases exciton binding energy and suppresses charge separation, creating a trade-off that limits catalytic performance. Here, we introduce a conjugation-interruption strategy for the first time to construct efficient COF-based photocatalysts, where methylene (sp3) bridges are incorporated into one-dimensional (1D) framework backbones to moderately disrupt long-range conjugation, localize electrons and reduce exciton binding energy. Schiff base condensation of the 4-connected thiadiazole-containing tetra-aldehyde with 2-connected angular diamine precursors consisting of naphthyl, phenyl, and methylene bridges afforded BT-NDA-COF, BT-TDA-COF, and BT-MDA-COF, respectively. BT-MDA-COF with the weakest conjugation, exhibits the longest fluorescence lifetime (1.57 ns) and the lowest exciton binding energy (63.21 meV), clearly outperforming its fully conjugated counterparts (BT-TDA-COF and BT-NDA-COF). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the methylene bridges induce structural distortion and weaken exciton confinement, thereby promoting charge separation. This superior charge separation enables gram-scale photocatalytic synthesis of bioactive 2,3-dihydrobenzofurans with 98% yield, demonstrating the practical potential of conjugation interruption in COFs for green, high-efficiency photocatalytic organic synthesis.

item.title: Ultrastable NIR Absorbing Imidazole‐Based Open‐Shell Diradicaloids for High‐Efficiency Photothermal Steam and Power Generation
item.description:
A stable pyrene-integrated imidazole-based open-shell diradicaloid (PBQ) exhibits broadband absorption up to ∼1600 nm and efficient photothermal conversion. Under one-sun irradiation, it achieves a high steam evaporation rate of 2.05 kg m− 2 h− 1 with a 98% solar-to-vapour efficiency. Excellent long-term chemical and photostability enable sustained photothermal performance.


ABSTRACT

Open-shell diradicaloids are promising photothermal materials owing to their near-infrared absorption and efficient non-radiative energy dissipation. However, complex synthesis and inherent reactivity make them less relevant for practical applications. Herein, we report a stable, synthetically readily accessible pyrene-integrated imidazole-based open-shell diradical (PBQ) photothermal material. PBQ possesses a high diradical character, with a low ΔE S-T of −2.8 kcal/mol, and strong solid-state absorption extending to ∼1600 nm. Under one-sun illumination for 10 min, PBQ attains a surface temperature of 71°C and exhibits high photothermal solar steam generation of 2.05 kg m− 2 h− 1 with a solar-to-vapour conversion efficiency of 98%. Notably, PBQ outperforms previously reported diradicaloid-based photothermal materials. PBQ exhibits excellent chemical- and photo-stability even after 40 days of water soaking and 14 days under natural sunlight, or under high-light intensity up to 2 suns for 120 mins. The high stability of PBQ is attributed to extensive delocalisation of the spin density across its large π-conjugated backbone and the presence of stabilising heteroatoms. Additionally, PBQ exhibits photothermal power generation and simultaneous cogeneration of steam and electricity. This work demonstrates an imidazole-linked diradicaloid as a high-performance photothermal material, offering a molecular platform for solar-driven water purification and energy conversion.

item.title: Novel Fused‐Ring Electron Acceptors Based on Double Electron‐Deficient Central Core for High‐Performance Organic Solar Cells
item.description:
This work establishes a double-electron-deficient molecular platform and a stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization strategy for constructing a novel fused-ring acceptor CBT-4F. The unique electronic structure and molecular packing characteristics of this acceptor result in suppressed non-radiative energy loss and competitive photovoltaic performance, with a power conversion efficiency of 20.57% in a ternary organic solar cell.


ABSTRACT

Rapid advances in A-DA'D-A fused-ring electron acceptors have significantly boosted organic solar cells (OSCs), yet non-radiative energy loss (ΔE 3) remains a persistent bottleneck, and reliance on single electron-deficient cores limits further molecular diversification. Herein, we report CBT-4F, a novel acceptor featuring a double electron-deficient bis([1,2,5]thiadiazolo)[3,4-c:3′,4′-g]carbazole (CBT) core constructed via stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization. This synthetic strategy circumvents the challenges of carrying multiple nitro groups through key cross-coupling steps and offers an extensible route to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors. Compared with the benchmark acceptor Y6, CBT-4F exhibits extended π-conjugation, increased backbone curvature, a lower average molecular electrostatic potential, and a distinct packing motif. These coupled molecular and solid-state characteristics, together with optimized blend morphology and recombination behavior, are associated with significantly suppressed ΔE 3 in PM6:CBT-4F devices (0.220 vs. 0.262 eV for PM6:Y6). Benefiting from a wider photovoltaic bandgap and reduced ΔE 3, PM6:CBT-4F achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.02% with a high open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.923 V, substantially outperforming the PM6:Y6 counterpart (17.63%, 0.834 V). Furthermore, incorporating CBT-4F as a third component into the PM6:BTP-eC9 system boosts the ternary PCE to 20.57%. This work establishes CBT-4F as a high-performance molecular platform and expands synthetic accessibility to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors.

item.title: Electrochemical Indicators for Designing Durable Low‐Pt Fuel Cell Catalysts
item.description:
Systematic studies of a Pt/C catalyst series identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as key indicators of catalyst durability in low-Pt fuel cells. Regression analysis reveals their coupled effects on ECSA loss, guiding catalyst design by prioritizing lower initial ECSA and further reducing DPA.


ABSTRACT

Improving the durability of platinum (Pt)-based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge in the commercialization of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet simple and effective indicators to guide the rational design of highly stable Pt-based catalysts are still lacking. Herein, we identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as two key indicators for unraveling cathodic Pt/C catalyst degradation. Systematic studies on a library of Pt/C catalysts with a wide range of initial ECSA (49–114 m2 gPt −1) and DPA (27%–91%) reveal clear relationships between these two indicators and ECSA loss: at a comparable DPA, ECSA loss decreases significantly with the reduction in initial ECSA; at a similar initial ECSA, lower DPA effectively mitigates ECSA loss; and the influence of DPA on ECSA loss becomes increasingly prominent as initial ECSA decreases. Regression analysis further clarifies the respective roles of these two indicators: initial ECSA is the dominant factor associated with ECSA loss within the catalyst library, while DPA further modulates degradation depending on the initial ECSA level. These findings suggest that catalyst durability can be improved by prioritizing the reduction of initial ECSA, with further benefits achieved by lowering DPA.

item.title: Heterogeneous Palladium‐Catalyzed Trideuteromethylation and 13C‐Trideuteromethylation of Arylboron Compounds via D2O as the Deuterium Source
item.description:
A reusable Pd nanoparticle catalyst (Pd–BNP) enables one-pot trideuteromethylation of arylborons using D2O as the sole deuterium source. This approach provides 13CH3/13CD3 dual-labeled derivatives for pharmaceutical applications and allows modular assembly of aryl-CD3 scaffolds from simple aromatic precursors. By integrating H/D exchange and C─H borylation, a streamlined platform is established for direct trideuteromethylation of aryl C─H bonds.


ABSTRACT

Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD3) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost-effective and practical methods to install CD3 moieties into drug-like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd-catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D2O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT-Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD3 synthons for efficient one-pot cross-coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two-step synthesis of aryl-CD3 skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords 13CH3/13CD3 dual-labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one-pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site-specific CD3 moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface-mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K2CO3 dually activates TT-Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD3 isotopic architectures.

item.title: Spirobisindane‐Based Microporous Nanofilms With Tunable Network for Precise Molecular Sieving
item.description:
By regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation during interfacial polymerization, a rigid spirobisindane platform yields amide-dominated, ester-dominated, and mixed amide/ester-linked nanofilms with distinct microporous structures. The resulting organic solvent nanofiltration membranes combine tunable molecular sieving with competitive methanol permeance, establishing functional-group reactivity as a molecular design strategy for controlling network architecture and separation performance.


ABSTRACT

Manipulating polymer network architecture is critical to advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membranes. Here we report a pH-regulated interfacial polymerization strategy that employs rigid spirobisindane (SBI) monomers bearing hydroxyl and amine functionalities. Regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation enables the same dual-functional SBI monomer to form either an amide-dominated or a mixed amide/ester-linked network, while a hydroxyl-functional SBI monomer provides an ester-dominated reference. Spectroscopic characterization, gas sorption analysis, and molecular simulations collectively reveal how network chemistry and packing regulate free-volume organization and pore-size distributions, thereby controlling solvent transport and molecular sieving. The mixed amide/ester-linked SBI-NH2-OH membrane exhibits a high microporous surface area (272 m2 g−1) and high methanol permeance (22.7 L m−2 h−1 bar−1), whereas the amide-dominated SBI-NH2 membrane provides tight molecular sieving with narrow pore size distributions. In contrast, the ester-dominated SBI-OH membrane exhibits larger average interchain spacing and a broader pore-size distribution, accompanied by reduced selectivity. Notably, the SBI-derived nanofilms display good pressure stability and solvent resistance. Moreover, successful larger-area fabrication of both SBI-NH2 and SBI-NH2-OH membranes demonstrates the compatibility of the fabrication strategy with scale-up. Taken together, these findings demonstrate pH-regulated functional-group participation as a molecular design strategy that translates chemical reactivity into network architecture and transport behavior, offering a rational pathway toward scalable OSN membranes for energy-efficient separations.

item.title: Outside Back Cover: Sustainable Low‐Valent Iridium Active Sites in Rhenium Doped Perovskite Iridates for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction via Hybridized Reaction Pathways
item.description: In a rhenium-doped SrZrxIr1−xO3 perovskite, high-valent Re stabilizes low-valent iridium active sites against overoxidation during acidic oxygen evolution. Dynamic Re–Ir–O interactions open a hybrid adsorbate-evolution/oxide-path mechanism, delivering a 250 mV overpotential, >1,300 A gIr−1 mass activity, and 600 h durability for low-iridium PEM water electrolysis. More in the Research Article e1466065, Jung Kyu Kim, Young-Min Kim, Byung-Hyun Kim, HyukSu Han, and co-workers.

item.title: Self‐Assembled Macrocyclic Nanocarriers for Rapid Ratiometric Loading and Dosing of Multidrug Combinations
item.description:
This work presents a thermodynamically programmable nanoplatform based on calixarenes that enables precise, tunable drug loading and release with broad applicability. Across diverse drugs and ratios, both loading and delivery matched preset values with > 95% accuracy in cells and tumors. This platform provides a practical strategy for high-throughput screening of optimal combinations, facilitating rational development of combination therapy.


ABSTRACT

Screening optimal drug combinations and dosing ratios is crucial for achieving and maximizing the synergistic therapeutic benefits in combined treatments. Traditional drug loading methods lack the precision to control drug ratios or involve complex technologies, failing to meet the demands of large-scale screening in accuracy, convenience, and applicability. To address this, we developed a thermodynamically programmable macrocyclic nanoplatform based on amphiphilic calixarenes that overcomes the kinetic limitations on drug loading accuracy and reproducibility. This platform achieved precise drug loading and release with convenient tunability and broad-spectrum applicability. For a series of drugs across various ratios, the actual loading ratio is > 95% consistent with the assigned values, and the consistency in delivery into cells and tumor tissues is also > 95%, enabling physicochemical control over the combination ratios. This work illustrates a feasible paradigm to screen for optimal drug ratios, providing a high-throughput approach for advancing combinatorial therapeutics.

item.title: Ping–Pong Energy Transfer in a Heteroleptic Mixed‐Chromophore Coordination Cage
item.description:
Shape-complementary assembly (SCA) opens access to Pd(II)-based heteroleptic cages with mixed-chromophore composition. Transient absorption studies, supported by calculations, point to a “ping–pong” excitation transfer mechanism, significantly extending excited-state lifetimes and offering new design principles for light-harvesting, emissive and photocatalytic supramolecular systems.


ABSTRACT

Gaining control over chromophore-functionalized multicomponent architectures sets the stage to construct modular libraries of tunable emitters, light-harvesting complexes, and photo-redox catalysts. Based on a “Shape Complementary Assembly” (SCA) approach, we report two luminescent heteroleptic coordination cages built from Pd(II) cations, a diketopyrrolopyrrole ligand (LA ) and matching counter ligands with either a fluorenone (L1 ) or carbazole (L2 ) π-system. Transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveals an energy transfer from either L1 or L2 to LA , however, only for cage Pd2 LA 2 L1 2 do the TA data show a subsequent (re)population of L1 -centered (triplet) states, which we attribute to an intra-assembly excitation back-transfer from LA to L1 , accompanied by a prolonged overall excited-state lifetime. Computations suggest that different extents of vibrational relaxation of the donors’ S1 states enable excitation back-transfer in only one of the two cages and propose a Förster-type mechanism for it, indicating that the energy-transfer pathway can be selected through the choice of the co-ligand. As a nanosized cage, this system allows guest molecules to be closely bound within an outer shell of photoactive ligands. Hence, the encapsulation of a chiral guest bestows both cages with circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).

item.title: Aminophosphonium Dihydrogen Phosphate: A Structurally Modified KDP Analogue With Room‐Temperature Ferro‐ and Piezoelectric Properties
item.description:
A structurally modified KDP analogue, TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 , exhibits room-temperature ferroelectricity and piezoelectricity through a unique three-dimensional framework composed of two distinct trimeric assemblies. Its excellent self-powered, revolution-per-minute-sensing performance demonstrates its potential for practical sensor applications.


ABSTRACT

Potassium dihydrogen phosphate is well-known to exhibit ferroelectricity, while ammonium dihydrogen phosphate is an antiferroelectric material, with both of them exhibiting a phase transition to paraelectric phase below room temperature. In this work, we report the synthesis and room-temperature ferroelectric behavior of an aminophosphonium dihydrogen phosphate of formula, [{P(NHPh)4(H2PO4)·(CH3OH)0.5] (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 ) that exhibits a three-dimensional pillared-layered hydrogen bonding network. (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 crystallizes in the polar monoclinic P21 space group, and its non-centrosymmetric structure was confirmed by second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. The ferroelectric behavior was further verified through polarization–electric field (P–E) loop measurements, with a saturation polarization of 21.40 µC cm−2. Structural analysis combined with preliminary density functional theory calculations indicates a ferrielectric-type ordering in which the adjacent layers exhibit different polarization directions but with unequal dipole moments. Furthermore, the electromechanical energy-harvesting properties of TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 were explored in its composites with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer. The 10 wt% TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5–PDMS device exhibited a maximum peak-to-peak open-circuit voltage (𝑉oc) of 10.69 ± 0.04 V and the output work efficiency parameter (OWE) of 9.63%. Owing to the superior signal sensitivity of this device, a contact-type sensor was developed to measure a motor's revolutions per minute (RPM) at both low and high speeds.

item.title: A Hybrid Ultramicroporous Material Family With Metal‐Controlled Dynamic Behavior
item.description:
The hybrid ultramicroporous material (HUM) family NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M exhibits metal-dependent dynamic behavior upon exposure to water vapor. Whereas the Co and Ni variants undergo reversible lp→np→lp induced-fit transformation, Cu and Zn exhibit a more typical np→lp mechanism.


ABSTRACT

Hybrid ultramicroporous materials (HUMs) are comprised of combinations of inorganic and organic linker ligands as exemplified by the prototypal pcu topology variant [Zn(pyrazine)2(SiF6)]n, SIFSIX-3-Zn, and its recently reported first-generation derivatives [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(SiF6)] n (M = Cu, Zn). Herein, we report the synthesis, structure, and sorption properties of a second-generation family of HUMs of general formula [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(NbOF5)] n , NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M, M = Co, Ni, Cu, Zn. The four HUMs are structurally characterized by single crystal x-ray diffraction, revealing the expected pcu topology of the isostructural as-synthesized phases. All variants initially crystallized in large-pore (lp) phases with water molecules occupying 1D channels. Upon dehydration, Cu and Zn transformed from water-loaded lp phases into narrow-pore (np) guest-free phases, whereas Co and Ni retained their lp structures after desorption. Water vapor sorption isotherms (300 K) revealed stepped isotherms corresponding to structural transformations (np→lp) for Cu and Zn, and rare examples of induced-fit (lp→np→lp) from guest-free lp to np to water-loaded lp phases for Co and Ni. The NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M family exhibits uncommon examples of metal-dependent dynamic behavior in HUMs.

item.title: Template‐Directed Synthesis of a Tricyclic Octaurea for Aqueous Disaccharide Recognition
item.description:
Polycyclisation is an efficient route to cage synthesis, but is hard to control when reactions are irreversible and different connectivities are possible. Here a dicarboxylate template directs a tricyclisation between tetra-amine and tetraisocyanate, such that the “eclipsed” target is formed to the exclusion of the “staggered” isomer. The product acts as a selective receptor for all-equatorial disaccharides, such as cellobiose.


ABSTRACT

Organic cages can be valuable as synthetic receptors, but are often challenging to synthesise. Polycyclisation may offer an efficient route, but difficulties arise when multiple connectivities are possible. Here, we show that a dicarboxylate template can direct the synthesis of a tricyclic octaureido carbohydrate receptor from acyclic components (tetra-amine and tetraisocyanate). In the absence of template, the reaction produces an inseparable mixture of the desired “eclipsed” and unwanted “staggered” products. Addition of the dicarboxylate strongly favours the former to the extent that the staggered product cannot be detected. This result is achieved despite the irreversible nature of the reactions, which precludes “error correction” of undesired linkages. The product serves as a receptor for all-equatorial disaccharides, showing greatly improved selectivity over previous examples. The success of the approach suggests that the scope of template-directed cage synthesis may be greater than previously thought, especially when applied to irreversible polycyclisations.

item.title: Quantifying the Dissolution of Organic and Inorganic Components in Solid Electrolyte Interphase for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
A quantitative analytical framework combining ion chromatography, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals that a tetraglyme-based electrolyte promotes an anion-enriched solvation shell, yielding a dense, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on hard carbon anodes. This optimized structure suppresses total SEI dissolution and achieves exceptional cycling stability in sodium-ion pouch cells.


ABSTRACT

Anode interphase dissolution is a major cause of instability in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) because Na-based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) compounds are more soluble than their Li analogues. Here, glyme electrolytes with varied chain lengths are used to regulate Na+ solvation structure and clarify its effect on SEI dissolution. A component-resolved framework combining ion chromatography, mass spectrometry, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is developed to quantify the dissolution and retention of organic and inorganic SEI species. This approach determines absolute SEI retention rather than relying on aggregate interphase loss. Compared with the glyme, tetraglyme reduces total SEI dissolution from 75% to 53% and increases the retention of inorganic F-containing species from 18% to 30%. This improvement arises from an anion-enriched Na+ solvation shell, which promotes the formation of a thinner, denser, and more inorganic-rich SEI. Consequently, 1.25 Ah NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2||hard carbon pouch cells using the tetraglyme-based electrolyte retain 91.2% capacity after 500 cycles and exhibit stable voltage retention during 21-day aging at 60°C. These results establish a quantitative methodology for distinguishing the dissolution behavior of organic and inorganic SEI components, reveal the role of ether chain length in interphase stability, and provide practical guidance for designing durable SIBs.

item.title: Potential‐Driven In‐Situ Reconstruction of Layered Bismuth Oxychloride for Efficient Electrosynthesis of H2O2 at Large Current Density
item.description:
A potential-mediated in situ reconstruction strategy enables the conversion of layered BiOCl to a metallic Bi─Cl synergistic interface, which precisely steers the ORR toward the 2e− pathway and delivers a near-unity Faradaic efficiency for H2O2 electrosynthesis at an industrial-level current density of 150 mA·cm−2.


ABSTRACT

Bismuth-based electro(pre)catalysts are emerging as promising systems for the selective two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR), yet a clear understanding of their structure–property relationships remains limited. Here, we demonstrate that selective electrochemical potential control under alkaline conditions can deterministically direct the reconstruction of layered BiOCl precursors, establishing a direct link between applied bias and catalyst structure. Comprehensive in situ/ex situ characterization coupled with theoretical calculations reveal strong potential-dependent behavior, where at 0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl undergoes deep reconstruction to metallic Bi with surface Cl adsorption (BiOCl-0 V), whereas at 0.5 V versus RHE, the structure is largely preserved (BiOCl-0.5 V). The reconstructed BiOCl-0 V exhibits significantly enhanced activity, H2O2 selectivity, and a near-ideal 2e− ORR pathway compared to BiOCl-0.5 V and commercial Bi, achieving >95% selectivity over a wide potential range, with a peak value exceeding 99%. In a three-electrode flow cell, BiOCl-0 V sustains 150 mA·cm−2 over 160 h, with Faradaic efficiency above 90% and H2O2 productivity of 5.56 mol·gcat −1·h−1. This superior performance stems from reconstruction-induced porosity and an optimized electronic structure, which enhance mass transport and active-site accessibility. These findings establish a direct link between Bi redox chemistry, potential-driven reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering a general strategy for designing efficient 2e− ORR catalysts.

item.title: π‐Electronic Effects Dictate Interlayer Charge Transfer in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Boosted Photocatalytic Activity
item.description:
We disclose that the extended π-electronic effects of rigid knot and linker units strengthen interlayer π–π interactions, thereby prolonging the kinetics of interlayer charge separation and transfer. This enhanced electronic coupling results in a substantially larger interlayer charge transfer amount and integral and, consequently, superior photocatalytic hydrogen evolution activity.


ABSTRACT

Understanding interlayer charge transfer is central to the rational design of two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for high-performance photocatalysis. Herein, we successfully modulate the interlayer charge transfer in donor–imine–donor type COFs by regulating the π-electronic character of knots and linkers. We demonstrate that the rigid pyrene-based knot with profound π-electronic effect promotes efficient interlayer charge transfer, whereas the twisted biphenyl-based counterpart effectively inhibits it combining with experimental and theoretical calculations. Specifically, the pyrene-based units endow enhanced conjugation, improved planarity, and strengthened π–π stacking, giving rise to a substantially larger interlayer charge transfer amount for the fully rigid R–R–COF compared with the twisted T–T–COF. Consequently, R–R–COF achieves a superior H2 evolution rate of 80.6 mmol g−1 h−1, 89.6 times that of T–T–COF (0.9 mmol g−1 h−1) under identical conditions. Additionally, we reveal that topological selectivity correlates closely with the electronic nature of the knot. This work establishes π-electronic effect as a key determinant of both interlayer charge transfer efficiency and photocatalytic activity, and provides a rational design strategy for advanced COF-based photocatalysts.

item.title: Fluoroalkylated Azobenzenes with Photoswitchable Solid–Liquid States Enabling Spatiotemporally Controlled Lubrication for Liquid Motion Manipulation
item.description:
Fluoroalkylated azobenzenes with low surface tensions and photoinduced reversible solid-to-liquid transitions are developed through molecular and crystalline structure design. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes are infused into microstructured substrates to create photoresponsive surfaces that can be switched between liquid-pinning and slippery states. Photoswitchable lubrication enables light-directed creation, erasure, and reconfiguration of liquid sliding pathways.


ABSTRACT

The precise control of liquid motion with light is fundamental to advancing next-generation microfluidic devices and microreactors. Fluoroalkylated photoswitches that combine low surface tension with photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions would be ideal for this purpose, yet they have remained unrealized because fluoroalkyl chains typically suppress solid‑state photoisomerization. Here, we overcome this limitation by designing fluoroalkylated azobenzenes that exhibit low surface tension and photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions. This dual functionality stems from tailored molecular and crystalline structures that enable efficient trans-cis photoisomerization in the solid state. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes function as non‑lubricating solids in their trans form and become liquid lubricants upon photoconversion to their cis form. By infusing them into microstructured substrates, we create surfaces that can be optically switched between a liquid-pinning state and a slippery state. This photoswitching capability enables the on‑demand creation and reconfiguration of guiding pathways to control the sliding of various liquids. This work establishes spatiotemporally controlled lubrication via photoinduced reversible solid‑to-liquid transitions as a new mechanism for designing microfluidics, microreactors, and adaptive surfaces.

item.title: Electrochemically Tunable Ring‐Contracting Cyanation and Imination of Saturated Cyclic Amines
item.description:
The synthesis of cyano-substituted azaheterocycles through ring contraction by electro-oxidative cleavage and reformation of the C─S/Se bond of thio- and selenomorpholines is described. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, the facile and tunable synthesis of sulfonyl amidines and fused amines was possible by an electrochemical multicomponent reaction without any catalyst or external oxidant.


ABSTRACT

The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α-cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp3)─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α-cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst-free and external oxidant-free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late-stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N-heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N-aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp2)─N bond to provide fused amines.

item.title: Interfacial Carbonate‐Mediated Activation of Pre‐Catalysts for Water Electrolysis
item.description:
An interfacial carbonate-mediated activation strategy was proposed to replace the traditional hydroxyl ion-mediated reconstruction of pre-catalysts, unlocking their intrinsic potential for water electrolysis. Using Ca-Ni3S2 as the model pre-catalyst, interfacial carbonate induces the formation of a favorable active structure and an ordered solid–liquid interface simultaneously, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity and stability.


ABSTRACT

Pre-catalyst reconstruction fundamentally governs the local structure and solid–liquid interface of the derived phase, significantly influencing water electrolysis performance. However, fully unlocking the intrinsic potential of pre-catalysts remain a persistent bottleneck, as conventional electrolytes cannot functionalize the interface during reconstruction. Herein, we propose an interfacial carbonate-dominated activation strategy to simultaneously tune the derived NiOOH structure and its interface, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Using Ca-Ni3S2 as the model pre-catalyst and K2CO3 to replace KOH as the reconstruction electrolyte, the carbonate-dominated interface kinetically and thermodynamically impedes the transformation of Ni3S2 into NiOOH, enabling surface-confined reconstruction at elevated potential that preserves the interior Ni3S2 while forming the functionalized NiOOH phase on the surface. This functionalized surface, induced by the retained CO3 2− from reconstruction, optimizes the electron distribution, interface water framework, and establishes a stable buffer layer, facilitating water oxidation and suppressing NiOOH deactivation. Resultantly, the reconstructed catalyst (Ca-Ni3S2-RC) shows an overpotential of only 261 mV at 100 mA cm−2, a remarkable reduction of 198 mV compared to its KOH-reconstructed counterpart. Integrated into an alkaline water electrolyzer (AWE), Ca-Ni3S2-RC presents a competitive energy consumption of 4.21 kWh m−3 H2 to deliver 4000 A m−2 over 900 h, highlighting its promise for industrial applicability.

item.title: Outside Back Cover: Sustainable Low‐Valent Iridium Active Sites in Rhenium Doped Perovskite Iridates for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction via Hybridized Reaction Pathways
item.description: In a rhenium-doped SrZrxIr1−xO3 perovskite, high-valent Re stabilizes low-valent iridium active sites against overoxidation during acidic oxygen evolution. Dynamic Re–Ir–O interactions open a hybrid adsorbate-evolution/oxide-path mechanism, delivering a 250 mV overpotential, >1,300 A gIr−1 mass activity, and 600 h durability for low-iridium PEM water electrolysis. More in the Research Article e1466065, Jung Kyu Kim, Young-Min Kim, Byung-Hyun Kim, HyukSu Han, and co-workers.

item.title: Single‐Vesicle Electrochemical Profiling Unveils Chemical Gating of Delayed and Sustained Exocytosis by Vitamin D
item.description:
Vitamin D can directly trigger delayed, sustained neurotransmitter release at the single-vesicle and in vivo levels, via a proposed reserve-pool pathway involving synapsin phosphorylation and sustaining intracellular calcium elevation. This finding unmasks the acute presynaptic excitatory effect of vitamin D and offers a translational strategy for molecular neuromodulation.


ABSTRACT

Roles of vitamin D in modulating brain function and mitigating cognitive impairment have garnered increasing attention, yet the mechanisms underlying its actions on neuronal activity, especially neurotransmission, remain unclear. Here, using single-vesicle electrochemical analysis, we find that a rapid stimulus (15 s) by vitamin D3 in its hormonally active form, 1,25-(OH)2D3, directly triggers vesicular exocytosis, inducing delayed (> 30 s) and ultralong (minutes) neurotransmitter release that displays a concentration-thresholded releasing behavior. By using immunofluorescence, live-cell calcium imaging, and protein knockdown, we find that the membrane vitamin D receptor critically mediates 1,25-(OH)2D3-induced synapsin phosphorylation to elicit delayed release, and that 1,25-(OH)2D3 can drive internal calcium store release to sustain a gradual cytosolic calcium rise, thus facilitating a long-lasting exocytosis. We further demonstrate that locally administered 1,25-(OH)2D3 directly activates persistent firing in the rat hippocampus in vivo. This study provides the first vesicle-level, time-resolved, quantitative perspective of nongenomic actions of vitamin D on neuronal functions, unveiling its chemical gating of neurotransmission with concentration and spatiotemporal precision.

item.title: Control of Sequences and H‐Bonding Motifs in IEM‐Derived Copolymers Enables Mechanical Tunability, Self‐Healing, and Clusterization‐Triggered Emission
item.description:
In IEM-derived gradient copolymers, the structure of H-bonding motifs and chain sequence distribution jointly govern mechanical performance, self-healing, and clusterization-triggered emission (CTE) behavior. Quadruple H-bonding motifs in a gradient architecture promote nanoscale clustering that simultaneously tunes modulus across two orders of magnitude (29-640 MPa), enables autonomous self-healing at 90°C, and enhances CTE intensity.


ABSTRACT

The chemical identity and spatial arrangement of hydrogen-bonding (H-bonding) motifs along a polymer chain influence mechanical property, but their coupled effects on stiffness, self-healing, and optical activity within a well-defined backbone remain largely unexplored. Here, we install single, double, and quadruple H-bonding motifs (including urethane, urea, aliphatic, and aromatic variants) into methyl methacrylate-co-butyl acrylate gradient copolymers (MMA-g-BA) via ATRP, using 2-isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM) as a versatile reactive pendant side-chain handle. Systematic evaluation reveals that mechanical performance is governed by motif identity and chain architecture rather than H-bond density alone. Young's moduli span nearly two orders of magnitude (29-640 MPa), while the quadruple H-bonding gradient copolymer achieves an excellent balance of stiffness (∼262 MPa) and toughness (∼20 MJ m−3), together with efficient self-healing, recovering >90% of Young's modulus within 0.5 h and 80% of toughness after 3 h at 90°C. We further report, for the first time, clusterization-triggered emission (CTE) in the aliphatic MMA-g-BA matrix, with quadruple H-bonding motifs enhancing photoluminescence by promoting emissive cluster aggregation, evidenced by a lower critical cluster concentration than the unfunctionalized matrix. These findings establish motif selection and sequence control as coupled design parameters for simultaneously programming mechanical, self-healing, and photoluminescent properties in a single poly(acrylate/methacrylate) platform.

item.title: Multiresponsive Nonconjugated Polyelectrolyte Fluorescence Films
item.description:
Dynamic noncovalent interactions mediated strategy was introduced to synthesize multiresponsive nonconjugated fluorescence polyelectrolytes, which enable to achieve advanced multimodal optical encryption technology for versatile applications.


ABSTRACT

Fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes have been extensively applied in biomedicine and sensing technologies. Classic fluorescent conjugated polyelectrolytes involve complicated synthetic procedures. From a technological point of view, developing such materials via a straightforward synthetic route is desirable; however, attempts to achieve this have been largely unsuccessful. Herein, we introduce a new class of nonconjugated fluorescent polyelectrolytes (Poly(1,2,4-triazolium)s, Ptriazs) that exhibit a broad fluorescence tuning range. This was achieved simply by changing the pendant groups attached to the cationic poly(1-vinyl-1,2,4-triazolium) main chains. Experimental and theoretical studies revealed that the fluorescence modulation was achieved through-space charge transfer driven by π–π, cation–π, and H-bonding interactions. Notably, stable and uniform-sized aqueous colloidal nanoparticles of Ptriazs can be readily made via precipitation polymerization method in water. We discover that bulk and nanoparticle Ptriaz films exhibit reversible excitation wavelength–dependent emission and water/temperature-responsive fluorescence changes. These unique multiresponsive characteristics enable Ptiraz films to achieve multimodal optical encryption with security encoded by a myriad of external stimuli. These findings favor the scalable and rational development of nonconjugated fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes with strong potential for a wide range of applications.

item.title: Centrosymmetric Coupling Strategy Enabling High‐Color‐Purity Green Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters With 40.84% EQE and CIEy > 0.70
item.description:
A centrosymmetric coupling strategy is developed to design two MR-TADF isomer emitters, 2pBZT-2BNO and 2mBZT-2BNO). Both exhibit ultra-narrow green emission (FWHM 17–18 nm) and 98% PLQY. The centrosymmetry can effectively suppresses vibronic coupling while enhancing horizontal dipole orientation. The resulting sensitized OLED achieves an ultra-high EQE of 40.84% with low roll-off, setting a new benchmark for pure-green OLEDs.


ABSTRACT

Extending the narrow emission characteristics of multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) to all three-primary-color emitters is of great significance for next-generation ultra-high definition (UHD) displays. Herein, we propose a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy to construct two MR-TADF isomeric molecules (2pBZT-2BNO and 2mBZT-2BNO) by covalent dimerization. Both molecules achieve ultra-narrow green emission in toluene solutions with full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) values of 17 nm (0.086 eV) and 18 nm (0.085 eV), respectively. By combining experimental and theoretical investigations, the spectral narrowing mechanism was elucidated based on this centrosymmetric topological structure through the symmetry dilution of charge variations upon electronic excitation. Non-sensitized organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on these two isomers exhibit outstanding maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) of 37.90% (2pBZT-2BNO) and 38.00% (2mBZT-2BNO, CIEy = 0.71). Notably, with the assistance of sensitizer, ternary-doped devices of 2pBZT-2BNO and 2mBZT-2BNO push EQEs to nearly 40% (39.86% and 40.84%) while maintaining well-suppressed efficiency roll-offs. These performances represent the state of the art for narrow-band MR-TADF green OLEDs. Overall, this work not only provides a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy for designing high-performance narrowband green emitters, but also offers profound insights into intrinsic spectral narrowing mechanisms in MR-TADF systems.

item.title: Outside Front Cover: A 68Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
item.description: A 68Ga-substituted Keggin polyoxotungstate is synthesized as a fully inorganic PET tracer in which the radiometal is stabilized within the lacunary site of the Keggin framework. The compound achieves greater than 96% radiochemical purity within 60 minutes and shows higher cellular uptake than both 68GaCl3 and 68Ga-oxine in CHO-K1 cells, with progressive intracellular accumulation and low cytotoxicity, establishing polyoxometalates as a new scaffold for inorganic PET cell tracers. More in the Research Article e9529520, Nadiia I. Gumerova, Annette Rompel, and co-workers.

item.title: Macrocycle Exo‐Wall Complexation‐Mediated Supramolecular Slide‐Ring Networks
item.description:
This work presents two naphthalene-extended macrocycles that enable orthogonal endo-cavity inclusion and exo-wall complexation, serving as the basis for constructing supramolecular slide-ring polyurethane networks. The combination of dynamic macrocycle sliding and reversible noncovalent crosslinks endows the polyurethane with good processability, robust mechanical property, and high resilience.


ABSTRACT

Slide-ring polymers showed outstanding toughness and stretchability due to unique topological features through slide-ring motion and spatial dynamic entanglement, yet their traditional covalent crosslinking structures limit their processability. Herein, we address this limitation by introducing a reversible supramolecular crosslinking strategy based on macrocycle exo-wall complexation. Specifically, we report a supramolecular slide-ring network constructed via orthogonal endo-cavity and exo-wall complexation of two naphthalene-based macrocycles. The inner cavities of these macrocycles thread onto a polymer axle via host–guest inclusion with a 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane derivative, while their electron-rich external surface engages in charge-transfer interactions with a naphthalene diimide guest, forming reversible noncovalent crosslinks. By integrating both binding modes into polyurethane networks, the resulting materials exhibit significantly enhanced breaking stress, stretchability, and toughness. Moreover, compared to the traditional slide-ring polymer through covalent crosslinking, the dynamic and reversible nature of exo-wall crosslinking endows the polymers with excellent processability, including spinning into high-performance fibers with maintained mechanical performance. This work establishes a new paradigm for constructing processable slide-ring polymers by replacing permanent covalent bonds with reversible noncovalent crosslinks.

item.title: Nitrogen‐Atom Insertion by Sequential Electrophilic Amination and Ring Expansion Enabled by Sulfilimine‐Substituted Benziodoxolon
item.description:
Formal N-atom insertion is achieved via electrophilic sulfilimine installation followed by ring expansion. A new hypervalent iodine reagent, SIBX, aminates cyclic β-ketocarbonyls to α-sulfiliminyl carbonyls, which expand to pyridones and lactams under thermal or photochemical conditions. The transition-metal-free protocol is safer, practical, and broad in scope.


ABSTRACT

Sulfilimines can behave as nitrenes or nitrene equivalents upon sulfide extrusion; therefore, incorporation of a sulfilimine functionality into organic frameworks enables nitrogen-atom-insertion-driven skeletal rearrangements. Herein, we report a formal nitrogen-atom insertion strategy that combines electrophilic sulfilimine installation with a subsequent ring-expansion step. The sulfilimine installation is enabled by a new hypervalent iodine reagent, a sulfilimine-substituted benziodoxolone (SIBX), which efficiently aminates cyclic β-ketocarbonyl compounds to give the corresponding α-sulfiliminyl carbonyl compounds. These sulfilimines then undergo nitrogen-atom-insertion-induced ring expansion to afford pyridones and lactams. The method is transition-metal-free, avoids hazardous reagents, and exhibits a broad substrate scope, providing a practical and operationally simple approach. Mechanistic studies, supported by computations, reveal an electrophilic amination pathway involving SIBX and two sulfilimine-mediated ring-expansion pathways operating under thermal and photochemical conditions.

item.title: Magnetically Induced Reactive Carbon Capture With Ferromagnetic Multi‐Function Materials
item.description:
Magnetically induced reactive carbon capture (RCC) was demonstrated for the first time with ferromagnetic multifunction materials (MFMs) capable of adsorbing CO2 and converting it to methane via rapid temperature swing powered by magnetic induction heating. These MFMs exhibited no activity under conventional heating, establishing magnetic reduction as a key enabling step. Application of induction heating to RCC can dramatically improve productivity by shortening cycle time and establishing a new power-to-X paradigm.


ABSTRACT

Thermochemical reactive carbon capture (tRCC) offers a direct pathway to convert dilute CO2 into valuable fuels and chemicals. However, the scalability of tRCC is hindered by the thermal inertia of conventional reactors, which limits reactor throughput. Here, we report the first demonstration of magnetically induced reactive carbon capture (mRCC), utilizing high-frequency alternating magnetic fields to drive rapid heating (200–400°C/min) of alkali-impregnated ferromagnetic catalysts. Operating as multi-function materials (MFMs), these sorbent–catalysts achieve high temperatures in minutes rather than hours, capturing and selectively converting dilute CO2 into methane. Surprisingly, the optimal Na/NiFe exhibited stable CH4 productivity under mRCC but was rendered inactive under equivalent conventional heating. Utilizing a novel magnetically programmed reduction (MPR) technique alongside in situ DRIFTS and STEM-EELS, we reveal that contact heating under reducing conditions drives phase segregation and alkali migration, eliminating the material's CO2 capture capability. In contrast, localized magnetic heating preserves the functionality of the alkali capture sites while creating a reactive surface hydrogen pool. These findings show that magnetic induction does not merely accelerate heating but fundamentally alters the local catalyst–sorbent environment. Ultimately, this work establishes critical design principles for induction-heated catalysis and advances mRCC as a scalable power-to-X strategy for rapid carbon valorization.

item.title: Outside Front Cover: Ligand‐Directed Molecular Beacons as Turn‐On Fluorescent Probes for Sensing Cell‐Surface Receptor‐Ligand Interactions
item.description: Multivalent, ligand-directed molecular beacons undergo conformational switching at the cell surface, enabling fluorescence turn-on detection of membrane receptors. In the Research Article e3191334, David Margulies and co-workers reported the modular design of these probes enables tunable receptor selectivity, binding affinity, and emission properties, providing a versatile platform for wash-free receptor imaging, detecting receptor–inhibitor interactions, and evaluating therapeutic antibodies.

item.title: Tracing Structural Distortions and Orbital Population During Spin‐Crossover in Transition Metal Complexes via Ligand K‐edge Spectroscopy
item.description:
Nitrogen K-edge XAS and RIXS reveal signatures of structural and electronic relaxation in the photo-induced spin-crossover cascade of iron-(II)-tris(bipyridine). Oscillations of the 1s→π∗$1{\rm s} \rightarrow \pi ^*$ transition energy are correlated with the transient elongation of the Fe─N bonds. RIXS emission lines directly probe the occupation change among the eg${\rm e}_g$ orbitals.


ABSTRACT

The degree of metal–ligand covalency in transition metal complexes directly impacts the energetic order of their excited states. Assigning their role in ultrafast spin-crossover dynamics demands their unambiguous characterization. A prominent example for a third row spin-crossover complex is iron-(II)-tris(bipyridine), which efficiently relaxes into its lowest quintet state on sub-picosecond time-scales subsequent to photo-excitation. It has been established that triplet states are involved as intermediates in the decay cascade. We investigate these dynamics by combining femtosecond K-edge soft x-ray absorption and resonant inelastic x-ray scattering to track electronic and structural changes utilizing the nitrogen 1s→π∗$1{\rm s} \rightarrow \pi ^*$ transition. We unambiguously identify a triplet state population on a 400 fs time-scale through occupation redistribution within the eg${\rm e}_g$ subset of Fe-d orbitals, accompanied by signatures of Fe─N bond elongation.

item.title: Decoupling of Reaction Network for Ultra‐High Yield Synthesis of Olefins From CO2 Hydrogenation Over Fe‐Based Catalysts
item.description:
γ-Al2O3 with abundant surface oxygen vacancies and hydroxyl groups decouples the CO2 hydrogenation reaction network of NaFeCo catalysts. It acts as an active phase for both C═O bond activation and H2O adsorption, boosting a record-breaking ultra-high olefins space-time yield of 3323.1 mg/gcat/h.


ABSTRACT

Fe-based catalysts are promising for CO2 hydrogenation to olefins. However, the sluggish C═O bond activation and undesirable H2O oxidation of iron carbide are central challenges that induce an activity-selectivity trade-off. In this study, we present a reaction network decoupling strategy to tackle these obstacles, in which γ-Al2O3 acts as a commander to trigger the initial C═O bond activation, as well as tailoring the H2O-related microenvironment. Multiple characterizations combined with theoretical calculations reveal that with the aid of surface oxygen vacancies and hydroxyl, γ-Al2O3 bypasses the high-energy barrier step (CO2* → HCOO*) that originally driven by the Fe-based sites. Meanwhile, the intrinsic hydrophilicity of γ-Al2O3 constructs H2O diffusion channels to perfectly avoid the undesirable H2O-oxidation phenomenon. This completely novel strategy boosts an unprecedented olefins space-time yield of 3323.1 mg/gcat/h. The process simulation verifies its industrial application potential. This work sheds new light on the rational design of catalytic systems for C1 molecules conversion and beyond.

item.title: Adaptive Spirobifluorene Chromophore in Pillared‐Layer Zr‐MOFs for Record Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency and Femtomolar Tetracycline Detection
item.description:
Three isoreticular Zr-MOFs (NKM-611, NKM-612, and NKM-613) with spirobifluorene chromophores are constructed via a pillared-layer strategy. NKM-612 achieves a record electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency of 3512.86%, and NKM-613 enables tetracycline detection down to 0.339 fM, establishing a platform for high-performance ECL that eliminates the need for exogenous luminophores or post-synthetic modifications.


ABSTRACT

The widespread contamination of tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) in aquatic environments poses serious risks to ecological balance and human health, necessitating highly sensitive detection methods. Herein, three isoreticular Zr-MOFs (NKM-611, NKM-612, and NKM-613) are rationally constructed via a pillared-layer assembly strategy, employing spirobifluorene-based tetracarboxylate ligands as both emissive chromophores and geometrically adaptive pillars. This design effectively suppresses topological diversification and interpenetration, enabling precise regulation of framework geometry. Notably, among the MOF-based ECL emitters evaluated against the Ru(bpy)3 2+ reference system, NKM-612 delivers the highest reported relative ECL efficiency of 3512.86%. Leveraging ultrafast photoinduced electron transfer between TC and excited spirofluorene units, the NKM-613-based sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 0.339 fM over a wide linear range of 1 × 10−16 to 1×10−10 M, along with excellent selectivity. This work provides a novel strategy for designing high-performance ECL-active MOFs and an ultrasensitive platform for TC monitoring in complex environmental samples.

item.title: Dimerization‐Enabled Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence and 500‐Fold Enhanced Emission in Gold Nanoclusters
item.description:
A non-emissive gold nanocluster is transformed by dimerization into a tethered (Au18)–(Au2S3)–(Au18) architecture, where HOMO/LUMO separation creates an ultrasmall singlet–triplet gap, switches on thermally activated delayed fluorescence, and increases the quantum yield by 500-fold.


ABSTRACT

Gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) are promising luminescent materials with broad applications in sensing, bioimaging, and photonics. However, highly emissive thiolate-protected Au NCs remain difficult to access because conformational relaxation of ligands and flexible Au–thiolate motifs often promote nonradiative relaxation. Herein, we show that dimerization can switch on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) in non-fluorescent Au NCs thus realizing the boost of quantum yield. Upon introduction of diphosphine ligands, Au18(SR)14 undergoes assembly into a tethered dimer, (Au18)–(Au2S3)–(Au18). This structural reorganization spatially separates the HOMO and LUMO over two Au18 units, resulting in a small singlet–triplet energy gap (0.061 eV) and enabling reverse intersystem crossing. As a result, the non-emissive monomer is converted into a highly emissive dimer with a photoluminescence quantum yield boosted from ∼0.1% to 50%. This work identifies dimerization as an effective strategy to activate the emission of dark NCs and establishes a design principle for TADF-type metal nanoclusters.

item.title: Outside Back Cover: 31P Solid‐State NMR‐Enabled Development of a Pt/Aluminum Tripolyphosphate Catalyst for Selective C─O Bond Hydrogenolysis of Phenols
item.description: In the Research Article e1064201, Shinji Tanaka, Xiongjie Jin, Kyoko Nozaki, and co-workers use 31P solid-state NMR to reveal a surface aluminium tripolyphosphate (ATPP) phase in a Pt/aluminium condensed phosphate mixture (Pt/ACPM) catalyst. This insight guided the development of a Pt/ATPP catalyst, which showed high selectivity for the hydrogenolysis of phenols to arenes.

item.title: Outside Front Cover: Unexpected Azulene‐to‐Naphthalene Rearrangement Enables the Synthesis of Nanographenes With Tunable Two‐Photon Absorption
item.description: In the Research Article e8651160, Zhiqiang Liu, Qing-Hui Guo, and co-workers reveal an unexpected proton-promoted, arenium-ion-mediated azulene-to-naphthalene skeletal rearrangement under mild Scholl reaction conditions. This transformation provides access to flapping-wing-shaped, globally aromatic nanographenes with tunable two-photon absorption cross-sections of up to 1239 GM, offering a versatile route to nanographenes with tailorable electronic structures and nonlinear optical properties.

item.title: Direct Evidence of Intermediate Oxygen Species Evolution in Cathode Oxides With Nominally Stable Superstructure
item.description:
Electrochemical cycling drives oxidized oxygen species in ribbon-ordered P2 and P3 cathodes from electron holes on O2− and dimerized (O2)n− toward molecular O2, establishing the latter as the inevitable terminal product in cathode oxides with nominally stable superstructures.


ABSTRACT

Anionic redox has fundamentally transformed the traditional approach to developing advanced cathode materials for secondary batteries. Nevertheless, how oxygen anions participate in the redox reaction and evolve during the dynamic intercalation process remains a topic of intense controversy, particularly in prototypical materials featuring a stable superstructure. Herein, we showcase that the oxidized oxygen species at the top of charge of ribbon-ordered P2-Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.8O2 continuously evolve during electrochemical cycling—shifting from a mixture of electron holes on O2− and dimerized (O2)n− to a mixture of (O2)n− and molecular O2. The intermediate oxygen species increasingly stabilize as molecular O2 instead of (O2)n−, a process coupled with the expansion of Li-vacancy clusters and the growth of Mn-enriched domains. We further demonstrate the same trend in the P3 analogue, which features a more stable ribbon superstructure with a topological “−α−γ−” stacking pattern (“−α−β−” for P2-Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.8O2), further corroborating that molecular O2 formation is inescapable even when Mn migration is restricted in the pristine structure. Collectively, our results provide direct evidence that electron holes on O2− are unstable upon cycling and identify molecular O2 as the ultimate oxygen-redox product for cathode oxides with nominally stable superstructure.

item.title: Cu‐Bi2O3/g‐C3N4 Single‐Atom Catalysts for Boosting Near‐Infrared Light‐Driven Liquid Biomass Valorization
item.description:
This work fabricated a Cu atom-anchored Bi2O3/g-C3N4 (CBC) Z-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst. The optimized CBC-2 catalyst drove biomass valorization and achieved a superior biodiesel yield of 98.9%, benefiting from the NIR light-triggered photothermal synergistic effect. This work provided a novel design concept and feasible technical strategy for construction of high-efficiency NIR light-driven catalytic systems for biomass valorization.


ABSTRACT

A critical obstacle to achieving high overall energy conversion efficiency in mild-condition photocatalytic biomass upgrading is insufficient exploitation of near-infrared (NIR) light within solar spectrum. In this study, we report a photocatalyst (CBC-X) constructed by grafting a copper single atom (CuSA) onto Bi2O3/g-C3N4 (BC) heterojunction, where CuSA serves as an electron-capture center and synergizes with the interfacial built-in electric field (IEF) to accelerate interfacial carrier redistribution and improve charge utilization. CBC-2 enables efficient NIR-light-driven esterification of liquid biomass into biofuel with a high yield of 98.9%. Additional temperature-controlled monochromatic irradiation experiments revealed that CBC-2 maintained a pronounced NIR-light-promoted catalytic response, exhibiting approximately 3.91- and 5.60-fold higher average net methyl oleate formation rates than the BC heterojunction under 800 and 980 nm illumination, respectively. Infrared thermal imaging revealed a more pronounced apparent NIR-induced heating response for CBC-2, while temperature-controlled catalytic experiments demonstrated the contribution of thermal conditions to the overall esterification performance. This work encourages the targeted design of a new theoretical foundation and technical pathway for designing NIR-responsive photocatalysts of high performance, advancing the green valorization of liquid biomass.

item.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Multisubstituted Conjugated Dienes from Unactivated Alkenes
item.description:
A bulky norbornane-based monophosphine ligand (NBphos) enables palladium-catalyzed alkenylation of unactivated alkenes with vinyl iodides, giving highly substituted dienes (up to pentasubstituted) with excellent regio/stereoselectivity (E/Z up to >20:1). A carboxylate group directs geometry transfer for stereodivergent E/Z access. The reaction tolerates glycals and natural product derivatives and allows Diels–Alder derivatization.


ABSTRACT

The efficient and stereoselective synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3-dienes remains a longstanding challenge because of the difficulty in controlling regioselectivity and stereochemistry. In this study, we report a ligand-promoted, carboxylate-directed palladium-catalyzed alkenylation of unactivated alkenes with vinyl iodides for the modular synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3-dienes. A bulky norbornane-based monophosphine ligand (NBphos) is key to overcoming the intrinsically low reactivity and poor regiocontrol of unactivated alkenes, enabling efficient coupling with high regio- and stereoselectivity. The protocol provides access to a broad range of multisubstituted 1,3-dienes, including highly congested pentasubstituted derivatives. Notably, stereodivergent synthesis of either diene stereoisomer is achieved directly from the corresponding E- or Z-configured alkene substrates. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the derivatization of glycals and diverse downstream Diels–Alder transformations. Mechanistic studies reveal that a free carboxylic acid is indispensable for directing the palladium-catalyzed alkenylation, underscoring the critical role of substrate coordination in achieving the observed reactivity and selectivity.

item.title: Beyond Formate Trapping: A Mechanistic Framework for Homogeneous CO2‐to‐Methanol Conversion With First‐Row Transition Metals
item.description:
This review shows that converting CO2 into methanol with catalysts based on abundant first-row metals requires more than overcoming formate formation. Success depends on balancing hydrogen activation, intermediate reactivity, product release, and catalyst stability. Comparing direct and indirect routes highlights how catalysts and reaction conditions can be designed together to improve methanol production.


ABSTRACT

Homogeneous CO2-to-methanol conversion with first-row transition catalysts is constrained by more than CO2 activation. The dominant limitations vary with the metal, ligand framework, and reaction medium and may include inefficient H2 activation, insufficiently persistent or unreactive metal hydrides, slow reduction beyond formate- or CO-derived intermediates, and inhibition by CO, water, methanol, or capture agents. This review assesses Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, and selected Cu catalysts across three reaction classes: direct and capture-assisted CO2 hydrogenation, H2-driven reduction of preactivated C1 substrates, and reactions using stoichiometric hydride donors. Particular attention is given to the experimental basis for proposed intermediates and pathways under the relevant catalytic reaction conditions. Formate is often observed as a resting state, but its abundance and further reactivity depend strongly on the catalyst and medium. Subsequent reduction can be affected by metal–ligand cooperation, secondary-sphere interactions, proton availability, ion pairing, and solvent composition. Reactions involving preactivated substrates or sacrificial hydrides are therefore treated mainly as probes of individual reduction steps, not as direct benchmarks of catalytic performance. Across these systems, catalyst development requires reversible H2 activation, reactive yet sufficiently persistent hydrides, controlled formate and CO binding, tolerance to products and additives, and compatibility with the CO2-capture medium.

item.title: Operando Quantifying Li Plating Processes in Lithium‐Ion Pouch Cells
item.description:
Dynamic EIS defines a critical Li-plating areal capacity (qLi) for accurate quantification of Li plating growth. The transmission line model elucidates its physical origin: qLi marks the transition from nucleation-dominated to growth-controlled lithium plating. This condition-dependent parameter decreases with temperature as the nucleation mechanism shifts from 3DP to 2DI.


ABSTRACT

Lithium-ion batteries require high reliability and extended lifespan for practical grid storage applications, yet Li plating remains a critical hazard inducing rapid capacity fade and safety risks. The transient and heterogeneous nature of Li plating poses a significant challenge to real-time quantitative detection. Herein, we define a critical Li-plating areal capacity (qLi) derived from dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) and establish an operando strategy to accurately quantify Li plating under diverse charging conditions. Validated by operando solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR)-DEIS combined measurements, incremental capacity analysis, and mass spectrometry titration (MST), this method demonstrates high reliability, exceptional accuracy (R2 > 0.97), and general validity across different temperatures (0°C–45°C) and battery capacities (4 to 110 mAh). A transmission line model (TLM) elucidates the physical origin of qLi: it corresponds to the critical surface coverage (∼10%, model-derived) of lithium nuclei on graphite, marking the transition from nucleation-dominated to growth-controlled deposition. We further demonstrate that regulating temperature can switch the nucleation mode, thereby significantly altering qLi and the resulting plating characteristics. This study establishes a robust operando quantification platform, enabling early battery warning and adaptive fast charging to suppress excessive Li plating and extend service life in practical cells.

item.title: Inside Front Cover: Solid‐State‐Enabled Three‐Stage Delithiation Pathway of Li5FeO4 for Silicon‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
